title: Gluten-Free Pistachio Rose Cupcakes
shortDescription: Gluten-free pistachio cupcakes with rosewater frosting, ready in about 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes baking.
description: These cupcakes use ground pistachios and almond flour for a moist, gluten-free crumb. Rosewater frosting keeps things light and floral, not soapy or heavy.
ingredients: 1 cup shelled unsalted pistachios, finely ground
1/2 cup unsalted butter, melted and cooled
1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
Crushed pistachios and dried rose petals, for garnish
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a muffin pan with 12 cupcake liners.
Whisk ground pistachios, almond flour, gluten-free flour blend, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
In a separate bowl, beat eggs and sugar until pale and slightly thick, about 2 minutes.
Add melted butter, milk, and vanilla to the egg mixture. Whisk until smooth.
Fold the dry mix into the wet mix in two additions. Stop as soon as no dry streaks remain.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two-thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
Beat softened butter until creamy, then add powdered sugar in two batches, mixing well after each.
Add rosewater and heavy cream. Beat 2 more minutes until light and fluffy.
Once cupcakes are fully cool, pipe frosting in a tall swirl on top. Garnish with crushed pistachios and rose petals.
tips: Grind pistachios in short pulses so they turn into fine meal, not paste. A food processor works better than a blender here.
Start with 1 teaspoon of rosewater and taste before adding more. Brands vary a lot in strength.
Let cupcakes cool completely before frosting. Warm cupcakes will melt the butter and cause the swirl to slide.
For a holiday look, add a few gold sugar pearls next to the rose petals.

faq.question: Can I use pistachio paste instead of ground pistachios?
faq.answer: Yes, swap in 1/3 cup pistachio paste and reduce the milk to 1/4 cup. The batter will be slightly denser but still moist.

faq.question: How strong should the rosewater taste be?
faq.answer: It should be a soft floral note in the background, not the first thing you taste. Start with 1 teaspoon and add more only after tasting the frosting.

faq.question: Can I make these dairy-free too?
faq.answer: Yes, use a plant-based butter and swap the milk and cream for full-fat coconut milk. Texture stays soft, though the crumb will be slightly denser.

faq.question: Why did my cupcakes turn out dense instead of light?
faq.answer: This usually happens if the pistachios were ground too fine into a paste, or if the batter was overmixed. Fold gently and stop as soon as the flour disappears.

conclusion: These cupcakes bring a soft pistachio crunch and a floral finish that feels right for holiday tables. Keep the rosewater light and the crumb will stay the star.
